- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward → reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots → cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward by 3–5% if sentiment turns negative.
- If true outcome shows early mean reversion (first 5–7 days drop > 10% from peak), model overestimates persistence → reduce forecast slope in early days.
- When sentiment swings from negative to positive (e.g., +0.3 to +0.5), model often fails to adjust downward → reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days.
- If model forecast is > 75 and true outcome is < 70, model overestimates volatility → reduce forecast by 10–15% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates downward trend after negative sentiment → add 2–5% upward bias if sentiment recovers within 5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (avg > 0.2) and model forecast is flat, model underestimates upside → increase forecast by 3–5% if sentiment remains positive for 3+ days.
